steps.tx: Ian Taylor and Palmer originally formulated the **angiosome concept** to describe an anatomical three-dimensional block of human tissue supplied by an individual source artery with its companion paired veins. The body encompasses roughly 40 distinct angiosomes spanning skin, subcutaneous fat, deep fascia, muscle, and underlying skeleton.
steps.say: Surgeons identify that taylor and Palmer defined an angiosome as a three-dimensional block of tissue supplied by a source artery and companion veins. Surgeons identify that surgeons identify that the body contains forty distinct angiosomes across skin and deeper musculoskeletal tissues.

vis.alt: Anatomical angiosome boundaries and tissue plane dissection
vis.caption: Angiosome boundaries and fascial planes in reconstructive surgery. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.tx: Adjacent angiosomes communicate across boundary territories through two types of anastomotic vessels: **true anastomoses** without luminal caliber reduction, and **choke vessels** that exhibit narrowing and increased resistance. Flap survival across multiple angiosomes relies on the opening and dilation of these critical choke vessel interconnections.
steps.say: Surgeons identify that adjacent angiosomes communicate via true anastomoses without caliber changes, and choke vessels that exhibit luminal narrowing. Surgeons identify that surgeons identify that flap survival across angiosome boundaries depends on dilation of these choke vessels.

steps.tx: Modern **perforator flaps** isolate cutaneous and subcutaneous tissues nourished by individual perforating vessels arising from deep source vascular axes. Unlike traditional musculocutaneous flaps, perforator flaps spare the underlying source muscle entirely, significantly reducing donor site functional impairment, postoperative pain, and herniation risks.
steps.say: Surgeons identify that perforator flaps isolate skin and subcutaneous tissue based on individual perforating vessels arising from deep source arteries. Sparing the underlying muscle reduces donor site morbidity and prevents hernia formation.

vis.alt: Surgical dissection scalpel for perforator isolation
vis.caption: Precision dissection instruments for intramuscular perforator isolation. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.tx: Perforator anatomy categorises vessels based on their anatomical course through tissue planes. A **musculocutaneous perforator** traverses through muscle bellies before penetrating the deep fascia, whereas a **septocutaneous perforator** travels entirely within intermuscular fascial septa, allowing faster and less traumatic intramuscular dissection.
steps.say: Perforating vessels are classified by their tissue course. Surgeons identify that musculocutaneous perforators traverse muscle bellies, while septocutaneous perforators travel through intermuscular septa without splitting muscle fibers.

steps.tx: The **anterolateral thigh flap** or ALT serves as a premier versatile perforator flap in reconstructive surgery, based on skin vessels arising from the descending branch of the lateral circumflex femoral system. It provides supple pliable skin, substantial pedicle length, and large dimensions with minimal donor site morbidity.
steps.say: The anterolateral thigh flap serves as a workhorse reconstructive flap based on perforators from the lateral circumflex femoral artery. It provides pliable skin and a long vascular pedicle.

nodes.label: Lateral circumflex femoral artery descending branch
Septocutaneous or musculocutaneous perforator to thigh skin

steps.tx: The **deep inferior epigastric perforator** or DIEP flap is the premier choice for autologous breast reconstruction, based on periumbilical perforators piercing the anterior rectus abdominis sheath. By carefully dissecting perforators through the rectus abdominis without harvesting the muscle, abdominal wall integrity and rectus function remain preserved.
steps.say: The deep inferior epigastric perforator flap is the gold standard for autologous breast reconstruction, using periumbilical perforators. Surgeons identify that preserving the rectus abdominis muscle prevents abdominal bulge and hernia.

steps.tx: Preoperative **perforator mapping** optimizes surgical flap design and reduces operative time significantly. Modalities include handheld acoustic Doppler, high-resolution computed tomography angiography CTA, and magnetic resonance angiography MRA. Intraoperative indocyanine green fluorescence angiography visualises real-time capillary perfusion and boundary demarcation across the cutaneous territory.
steps.say: Surgeons identify that preoperative perforator mapping optimizes flap planning and operative safety using handheld Doppler, computed tomography angiography, and indocyanine green fluorescence imaging.

steps.tx: Perforator flaps can also be harvested as **propeller flaps**, rotated on a single eccentric perforator axis up to 180 degrees to reconstruct adjacent soft tissue defects with healthy matched skin. Ensuring meticulous circumferential skeletonization of at least 3 cm of pedicle length prevents mechanical torsion, kinking, and critical venous outflow obstruction during inset into complex regional wounds.
steps.say: Surgeons identify that propeller flaps rotate on a single skeletonized perforator up to one hundred eighty degrees to cover local defects. Surgeons identify that skeletonizing adequate pedicle length prevents mechanical torsion and venous obstruction.
